item.title: Data center switch market doubled in three years, hits record 3Q 2025 – Dell'Oro
item.description: Accton, Celestica and NVIDIA captured highest share gain. #pressrelease

item.title: E.W. Scripps board rejects Sinclair offer
item.description: The E.W. Scripps's board of directors has unanimously rejected Sinclair's unsolicited acquisition offer made on November 24, finding it 'is not in the best interests of the company and its shareholders.' #pressrelease

item.title: US fiber broadband deployments hit record 11.8M in 2025 – FBA
item.description: Fiber broadband deployments reached 11.8 million US homes in 2025, a new record, for a total of 98.3 million when including homes with more than 1 passing, according to the Fiber Broadband Association (FBA). #pressrelease

item.title: 2025 in review: China's inroads into Europe
item.description: Huawei has remained under pressure in Europe throughout the 5G era, and the walls have continued to close in this year.

item.title: 2025 in review: D2D rolls out
item.description: Light Reading's direct-to-device (D2D) market coverage this year spotlights a progression from testing to commercial launches, as well as the competitive dynamics among global satellite partners and the approaches embraced by mobile and cable network operators.

item.title: Eurobites: Ookla reveals big urban-rural divide in UK mobile quality
item.description: Also in today's EMEA regional roundup: VMO2 reports growing data use; Proximus CFO heads for the exit; BNetzA launches speed checking tool.

item.title: American Tower presses its case against Dish Wireless
item.description: American Tower has asked a court to enter a declaratory judgment on claims that Dish Wireless' tower contract remains in full force. Dish believes it is 'excused' from the contract in the wake of EchoStar's spectrum sales.

item.title: AT&T wins court order to stop T-Mobile's Easy Switch from taking its data
item.description: Federal judge orders temporary injunction to block part of T-Mobile's Easy Switch tool from accessing AT&T's data as litigation proceeds.

item.title: Optimum claims Tegna is demanding 'outrageous' price hike
item.description: Optimum, formerly known as Altice USA, claims Tegna, a broadcaster of certain ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC affiliates, and CW – is seeking price hikes in the range of 30% to 50%. #pressrelease

item.title: WBD board rejects Paramount offer, citing 'significant risks'
item.description: Warner Bros. Discovery's board has urged shareholders to reject Paramount's hostile takeover offer, claiming it's 'inferior' and rife with 'significant risks.' A bidding war between Paramount and Netflix may follow.
